<SUMMARY>
Global geopolitical and economic landscapes experienced notable shifts this week, largely driven by advancements in AI and semiconductor technologies, intensifying resource competition, and persistent regional conflicts. Huawei unveiled a new chip architecture aiming to bypass US sanctions, while the US moved to formalize trade agreements with Taiwan to bolster semiconductor supply chains. The ongoing conflict in Iran continued to disrupt global energy and commodity markets, particularly impacting aluminum supply and energy security. Concurrently, nations sought to secure critical mineral supplies, with India and Russia deepening rare earths cooperation and Türkiye targeting uranium reserves in Somalia. The rapid expansion of AI infrastructure spurred significant investments but also raised concerns over environmental impact and energy consumption, prompting regulatory discussions in Europe and the US.
</SUMMARY>
<EWS>
An escalating risk of global energy instability is evident, with the ongoing Iran conflict triggering a "serious and prolonged supply outage" in the aluminum market and threatening global oil security, as highlighted by the IEA. This situation is further complicated by the closure of the Strait of Hormuz, directly disrupting India's drug lifeline to Africa and emphasizing critical supply chain vulnerabilities. The rapid and unregulated growth of AI data centers poses an emerging environmental threat, with academic findings suggesting contributions to local warming, prompting regulatory responses like Italy's 200% tax on agricultural zone development. Furthermore, China's strong reaction to the Quad meeting concerning maritime affairs in its neighborhood signals potential regional naval tensions.
</EWS>
<EXEC>

**Asia:**
The Steam Deck, a portable PC gaming device, is back in stock but at almost double its original price, now costing $789 USD for the 512GB OLED version and $949 for the 1TB upgrade. SanDisk Corporation shares surged over 500 percent year-to-date due to booming demand for NAND flash memory from artificial intelligence data centers. AppLovin Corporation shares soared more than 12 percent to $576.41 after reporting robust first-quarter results and raising full-year guidance, highlighting continued strong AI advertising momentum.

**Africa:**
Uganda closed its border with Congo due to an Ebola outbreak that has caused more than 220 deaths, with efforts to control the spread hampered by ongoing violence and instability in Congo.

**Europe:**
The Dutch financial crimes agency raided data centers and seized 800 servers linked to Russian cyberattacks, underscoring increasing regulatory scrutiny on digital infrastructure. The Italian council set a 200% tax on data center development in agricultural zones, aiming to spur the use of old industrial areas and limit environmental impact. Mercury revenues reached €2 billion last year, boosting profits 13% to €136 million for the specialist builder. Shares of a European chip manufacturer soared 70% following a social media boost. Sanofi is building its own AI ecosystem to develop custom tools and reimagine AI workflows, rather than relying on agentic products from SaaS vendors. The global Metal Working Machinery Market is projected to reach USD 138.10 Billion by 2033, driven by CNC automation, precision manufacturing, and industrial capacity modernization.

**Americas:**
Brazilian Senator and presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro met privately with President Donald Trump at the White House. Environmental activist Erin Brockovich launched an online AI data center tracking project to document its environmental impact on local communities. Mexico and the EU signed a trade agreement at their first summit in over a decade, removing high tariffs on agricultural exports and opening new markets for food, pharma, and raw materials. Gavin Newsom is taking a populist turn on AI ahead of a possible 2028 presidential run, with AI becoming a dominant political issue. Elon Musk warned that the US must boost chip manufacturing for AI security and energy to maintain AI leadership amid geopolitical risks.
</EXEC>
<LITHO>

**Asia:**
Huawei's ‘Chip Queen’ indicated the Chinese company is adapting to the demise of Moore’s Law, which could complicate US chip dominance. Huawei’s Mate 90 series will use near-3nm chip technology based on a new Kirin processor using the Tao Scaling Law, promising major performance gains despite US sanctions. The US eased tariffs on Taiwan to formalize a trade agreement, strengthening semiconductor supply chains and boosting US tech sectors. Nvidia's investment in Taiwan signals a new AI supply chain reality. Huawei's workaround for US chip curbs faces hurdles on the road to self-reliance. China is training a domestic compute stack under export controls.

**Europe:**
ASML shares are up 53% in 2026. XFAB, focusing on photonics and power semiconductors, is seen as an interesting investment, with exposure to the EU CHIPS Act 2 as a catalyst for European photonics players.

**Americas:**
Huhutech won a $936,000 contract from a U.S. semiconductor foundry. Nexperia secured a US manufacturing partner for power MOSFETs. Samsung is expanding its U.S. Foundry Ecosystem. IBM spun off America's first quantum chip foundry, "Anderon," with $2 billion in federal and private funding, offering 300mm quantum wafer fab and manufacturing services. Lenovo's Yoga 7A 2-in-1 16 offers Ryzen AI performance.
</LITHO>
<REE>

**Africa:**
Türkiye is targeting Somalia’s 10,200-ton uranium reserves in an expanding critical minerals race in Africa. M23 Congo Rebels contribute to a critical minerals crisis threatening US supply chains.

**Americas:**
The U.S. tungsten supply chain is tightening, with a Nevada past-producer mobilizing drone geophysics and property-wide soil geochemistry toward drill-ready targets, eight months before the January 1, 2027 DFARS procurement cliff on Chinese-origin tungsten. Northisle Copper and Gold Inc. announced its board slate for the 2026 AGM.

**Oceania:**
The Copi Mineral Sands Project near the Victoria-NSW border received provisional approval from the New South Wales government, recognizing its global strategic importance.
</REE>
<GEO>

**Asia:**
The US eased tariffs on Taiwan to formalize a trade agreement, enhancing economic ties. China strongly reacted to a Quad Ministerial meeting, which expressed serious concerns over the East and South China Sea situations, urging "certain countries to stop interfering" in maritime affairs in its neighborhood. Huawei's new chip architecture aims to workaround US chip curbs.

**Americas:**
Mexico and the EU inked a trade deal before the USMCA review, aiming to remove high tariffs on agricultural exports and open new markets for food, pharma, and raw materials.

**Europe:**
The Dutch financial crimes agency raided data centers and seized 800 servers linked to Russian cyberattacks, underscoring increasing regulatory scrutiny on digital infrastructure and the need for compliance to avoid sanctions evasion.
</GEO>
<MILITARY>

**Asia:**
China strongly reacted to a Quad Ministerial meeting, which had expressed serious concerns over the East and South China Sea situations, stating that the situation in these seas is generally stable and urging certain countries to stop meddling in maritime affairs in its neighborhood. The South Korea-US Alliance is making necessary updates to a 70-year-old framework regarding OPCON transfer.

**Europe:**
Germany’s bid to build Canada’s next-generation submarines promises a massive $86-billion economic boost and up to 50,000 jobs over five years for Canada, tying Arctic defense to NATO integration. Britain's cyberspying chief warned that artificial intelligence is becoming an "unstoppable force" weaponized just below traditional warfare levels, with a specific warning about Russia.

**Americas:**
Germany’s bid for Canada's next-generation submarines promises an $86-billion economic boost and up to 50,000 jobs over five years, tying Arctic defense to NATO integration for Canada.

**Oceania:**
The U.S. launched 'Self-Defense' Strikes on Iran.
</MILITARY>
<CONCLUSION>

**Asia:**
The competition in semiconductor technology is intensifying, with Huawei's new chip architecture challenging US dominance. The US-Taiwan trade agreement aims to bolster supply chains, while China’s push for domestic AI compute stacks under export controls indicates a strategic pivot. Geopolitical tensions in maritime affairs persist, as China criticized the Quad's involvement in the East and South China Sea.

**Africa:**
The Ebola outbreak in Congo continues to be a humanitarian crisis exacerbated by regional conflict, while Türkiye's pursuit of uranium reserves in Somalia highlights increasing global competition for critical minerals on the continent.

**Europe:**
Regulatory actions are increasing in the digital infrastructure sector, as seen with the Dutch raid on servers linked to Russian cyberattacks and Italy's tax on data centers. The European semiconductor market is also gaining traction with rising shares for local manufacturers and the EU CHIPS Act 2.

**Americas:**
The US is focusing on bolstering its chip manufacturing and AI security, with President Donald Trump welcoming Brazilian presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro. Trade relations are being reshaped with the Mexico-EU deal.

**Oceania:**
Strategic mineral projects like the Copi Mineral Sands in Australia are receiving approval, underscoring their global importance amidst tightening supply chains. The US has launched 'Self-Defense' Strikes on Iran.
</CONCLUSION>
<INDIA>
India and Russia are deepening rare earths ties, signing agreements for joint research and development to produce high-purity metals and compounds and develop processing technologies. PepsiCo is updating its snack packaging in India for brands like Lay's, Kurkure, and Doritos to clearly display "No Artificial Flavours or Colours." The Coal India OFS was subscribed over eight times on day one, leading the government to exercise its greenshoe option as part of its broader disinvestment and public shareholding strategy. Cognizant is reportedly planning to reduce between 12,000 and 15,000 jobs globally, with India expected to bear the brunt of these layoffs. The fleet telematics market in India is projected to expand from USD 10.42 billion in 2025 to USD 21.95 billion by 2032, driven by the adoption of advanced telematics in commercial vehicles for deeper operational intelligence and efficiency. India's drug lifeline to Africa has been disrupted by the Iran war, as the fragile logistics corridor via Gulf states, crucial for connecting African patients with Indian pharmaceuticals, has been thrown into disarray due to the closure of the Strait of Hormuz.
</INDIA>
<WEST_ASIA>
The war in Iran is triggering a "serious and prolonged supply outage" in the aluminum market, causing a historic crisis with potentially devastating knock-on effects across sectors. The conflict and accompanying shipping bottleneck, including the closure of the Strait of Hormuz, are disrupting global energy security and supply chains, notably impacting India's critical pharmaceutical supply to Africa. Goldman Sachs reported that foreign official institutions, including China and Japan, sold Treasuries as the dollar rose over 2% during the US-Iran conflict in March 2026, linking a stronger dollar to reduced Treasury demand. President Donald Trump stated he would not be comfortable with Russia or China taking Iran's stockpile of highly enriched uranium. Iranians have begun to regain internet access after a monthslong shutdown, though heavy restrictions remain. President Trump indicated that Washington is not satisfied with Tehran's offers for a deal, stating Iran cannot 'out-wait' him, suggesting no sanction relief. BiomX appointed IDF Colonel (res.) Roy Timor-Rousso as Chief Business Officer to strengthen defense and security operations. The International Energy Agency (IEA) stated the Middle East conflict has deepened the global energy crisis, reshaping energy investment plans as disruptions focus on security. UAE retailers are turning to AI agents to drive faster decisions and smarter automation. The US launched 'Self-Defense' Strikes on Iran. Oil shortages threaten global energy security.
</WEST_ASIA>
<FINAL_CONCLUSION>
The next quarter will likely see a continued acceleration in the global AI and semiconductor arms race, with nations prioritizing self-reliance and supply chain resilience. Huawei’s architectural innovations and China’s domestic compute stack development will challenge existing US export controls, potentially necessitating further adjustments to trade policies. The ongoing Iran conflict is set to exert prolonged pressure on global energy and raw material markets, especially for aluminum and oil, leading to sustained price volatility and a re-evaluation of international shipping routes. Geopolitical competition for critical minerals will intensify, particularly in Africa, as major powers seek to diversify and secure their supply chains. The environmental impact of rapidly expanding AI infrastructure will become a more pressing regulatory concern, prompting increased scrutiny and taxation on data center development, especially in developed economies.
</FINAL_CONCLUSION>
